question: Can decision-relevant progressive observation stop materially earlier than full Game trajectory inspection without changing the eventual causal research target, and outperform a same-window-count naive/random baseline?

ownerEvidence.role: paired pre/post AF Loop 001 Game variants sharing the same Experience World Model packet protocol; pretrial seed ablation proved nominal seed strings do not change trajectory bytes
owner continuity pressure: progressive causal-window selector is too broad and AF Loop 002 should reduce selected windows while preserving decision-relevant events

evidenceTopologyHypothesis: interactive temporal trajectory with sparse causally decisive windows embedded in a short sequence; aggregate overview can locate pressure but not establish the causal research target
chosenOperatorPolicy: overview plus Agent-selected causal windows; after each evidence batch the Agent must name live alternatives and either request a window that could discriminate them or STOP with a bounded causal research target; no confidence threshold
alternativeOperatorPolicies: full six-Turn trajectory supplied before one semantic decision
same number of unique causal windows as progressive stopping but selected by a frozen naive/random policy

prediction.frontierChange: Progressive stopping should preserve the full-evidence causal research target on most unambiguous cases while reducing unique windows and Provider/context cost; its agreement should exceed or equal matched random selection, otherwise the stopping/operator prior should contract.

expectedSignals.falseEarlyStopRate: <=0.25 on cases with a stable full-evidence reference
expectedSignals.criticalEventCoverage: progressive should retain the mechanically tagged event classes needed by its chosen causal claim rather than merely minimizing bytes

budget.fixedTrajectorySeed: rf1-fixed-seed / seed identity is provenance-only on this deterministic path

stopCondition: STOP is admissible only when the Agent states a current causal research target, enumerates remaining live alternatives, and asserts that no currently available unobserved Turn window is expected to distinguish an alternative strongly enough to change that target; otherwise it must request a discriminating Turn. The experiment never stops on confidence alone.
falsifier: The chosen policy is not supported if it usually consumes nearly the full trajectory, has false-early-stop rate above 0.25 on stable-reference cases, performs worse than matched random at the same unique-window count without compensating closed-loop savings, or systematically misses mechanically tagged decision-relevant event classes that change the full-evidence target.
